title: Ezekiel Chapter 10 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 10 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 10 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 10.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 10, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: A sapphire stone appeared over the cherubims
The man clothed with linen was told to scatter coals of fire
The sound of the cherubims' wings was heard
The glory of the LORD went up from the cherub
questions.correctAnswer: A sapphire stone appeared over the cherubims
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:1 states that the sapphire stone appeared over the cherubims first in the chapter.

questions.question: What was above the head of the cherubims according to Ezekiel 10?
options: A throne that looked like sapphire stone
questions.correctAnswer: A throne that looked like sapphire stone
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:1 describes that above the head of the cherubims appeared as it were a sapphire stone, the appearance of the likeness of a throne.

questions.question: Who was commanded to scatter coals of fire over the city?
options: The voice of the Almighty God
questions.correctAnswer: The man clothed with linen
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:2 states that the man clothed with linen was commanded to fill his hand with coals of fire and scatter them over the city.

questions.question: From where was the man clothed with linen told to take fire?
options: From between the wheels, from between the cherubims
questions.correctAnswer: From between the wheels, from between the cherubims
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:6 records the command to take fire from between the wheels, from between the cherubims.

questions.question: Where did the cherubims stand when the man went in?
options: On the right side of the house
questions.correctAnswer: On the right side of the house
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:3 states that the cherubims stood on the right side of the house when the man went in.

questions.question: What filled the inner court when the man went in?
questions.correctAnswer: A cloud
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:3 says that the cloud filled the inner court when the man went in.

questions.question: Where did the glory of the LORD stand after going up from the cherub?
options: Over the threshold of the house
questions.correctAnswer: Over the threshold of the house
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:4 states that the glory of the LORD went up from the cherub and stood over the threshold of the house.

questions.question: What was the court full of after the glory of the LORD stood over the threshold?
options: The brightness of the LORD'S glory
questions.correctAnswer: The brightness of the LORD'S glory
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:4 explains that the court was full of the brightness of the LORD'S glory.

questions.question: How was the sound of the cherubims' wings described?
options: As the voice of the Almighty God when he speaketh
Like the sound of many horses
questions.correctAnswer: As the voice of the Almighty God when he speaketh
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:5 states the sound of the cherubims' wings was heard as the voice of the Almighty God when he speaketh.

questions.question: Who stretched forth his hand to take fire from between the cherubims?
options: The voice of the Almighty God
questions.correctAnswer: One cherub
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:7 says one cherub stretched forth his hand from between the cherubims to take fire.

questions.question: What appeared in the cherubims under their wings?
options: The form of a man's hand
questions.correctAnswer: The form of a man's hand
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:8 records that the form of a man's hand appeared under the cherubims' wings.

questions.question: The man clothed with linen went in between the wheels as commanded.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:2 states that the man clothed with linen went in between the wheels as commanded.

questions.question: The house was filled with the cloud when the glory of the LORD went up from the cherub.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:4 states the house was filled with the cloud as the glory of the LORD stood over the threshold.

questions.question: The man clothed with linen was told to scatter coals of fire on the cherubims.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:2 states he was told to scatter coals of fire over the city, not on the cherubims.

questions.question: The scripture mentions that the cherubims had wings like those of a lion.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text in Ezekiel 10:1-8 does not mention the cherubims having wings like those of a lion.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 10 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 10 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What was the appearance of the wheels by the cherubims?
options: As the colour of a beryl stone
As the colour of a sapphire stone
questions.correctAnswer: As the colour of a beryl stone
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:9 states that the appearance of the wheels was as the colour of a beryl stone.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 10:2 promise will happen if someone does what verse 10:1 commands?
options: The glory of the LORD will leave
The city will be filled with coals of fire
The inner court will be filled with a cloud
questions.correctAnswer: The inner court will be filled with a cloud
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:4 indicates that when the glory of the LORD went up, the house was filled with a cloud.

questions.question: How did the cherubims move according to Ezekiel 10:11?
options: They went upon their four sides
They moved only in one direction
questions.correctAnswer: They went upon their four sides
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:11 describes that when they went, they went upon their four sides.

questions.question: What do the wheels follow according to Ezekiel 10:11?
options: The commands of the man clothed with linen
questions.correctAnswer: The head's direction
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:11 explains that they turned not as they went, but to the place whither the head looked, they followed it.

questions.question: What were the wheels full of according to Ezekiel 10:12?
questions.correctAnswer: Eyes round about
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:12 states that their whole body, and the wheels, were full of eyes round about.

questions.question: What was cried unto the wheels in Ezekiel 10:13?
questions.correctAnswer: O wheel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:13 records that it was cried unto the wheels, 'O wheel.'

questions.question: What faces did each cherub have according to Ezekiel 10:14?
questions.correctAnswer: Four faces
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:14 states that every one had four faces.

questions.question: What did the cherubims do when they lifted up their wings according to Ezekiel 10:16?
options: The wheels turned not from beside them
They called out to the man
questions.correctAnswer: The wheels turned not from beside them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:16 indicates that when the cherubims lifted up their wings, the same wheels also turned not from beside them.

questions.question: What was Ezekiel’s observation regarding the cherubims by the river of Chebar?
questions.correctAnswer: They were lifted up
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:15 mentions that the cherubims were lifted up.

questions.question: How did the sound of the cherubims’ wings compare according to Ezekiel 10:5?
options: Like the voice of the Almighty God
questions.correctAnswer: Like the voice of the Almighty God
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:5 states that the sound of the cherubims' wings was heard as the voice of the Almighty God.

questions.question: What practical lesson can be drawn from the movement of the wheels and cherubims?
questions.correctAnswer: Follow God's direction
questions.explanation: The unity in movement between the wheels and cherubims exemplifies the importance of following God's direction in our lives.

questions.question: What should one remember about the vision of the cherubims when facing challenges?
options: God’s glory can fill any space
questions.correctAnswer: God’s glory can fill any space
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:4 shows that when the glory of the LORD went up, the house was filled with the brightness of the LORD'S glory, indicating God's omnipresence.

questions.question: Is it true that the cherubims have multiple faces according to Ezekiel 10:14?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:14 clearly states that every one had four faces, confirming the truth of the statement.

questions.question: Is it false that the wheels have the same appearance as the cherubims according to Ezekiel 10:10?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:10 indicates that the appearances were similar as if a wheel had been in the midst of a wheel, making the statement false.

questions.question: Is it false that the wings of the cherubims are heard in the outer court according to Ezekiel 10:5?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:5 states that the sound of the cherubims' wings was heard even to the outer court, indicating the statement is false.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 10 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 10.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 10:17, what caused the wheels to lift themselves when the living creatures lifted up themselves?
options: The spirit of the living creature was in them
The sound of the cherubims' wings
The glory of the LORD was upon them
The fire scattered over the city
questions.correctAnswer: The spirit of the living creature was in them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:17 states explicitly that 'for the spirit of the living creature was in them,' explaining why the wheels lifted themselves when the creatures did.

questions.question: What happened to the glory of the LORD according to Ezekiel 10:18?
options: It departed from off the threshold of the house and stood over the cherubims
It covered the city with fire
It remained above the river of Chebar
questions.correctAnswer: It departed from off the threshold of the house and stood over the cherubims
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:18 clearly records that 'the glory of the LORD departed from off the threshold of the house, and stood over the cherubims.'

questions.question: In Ezekiel 10:19, where did the cherubims stand after mounting up from the earth?
options: At the door of the east gate of the LORD'S house
In the inner court of the house
questions.correctAnswer: At the door of the east gate of the LORD'S house
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:19 states that after the cherubims mounted up, 'every one stood at the door of the east gate of the LORD'S house.'

questions.question: How many faces did each cherubim have according to Ezekiel 10:21?
questions.correctAnswer: Four faces apiece
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:21 says 'Every one had four faces apiece,' confirming the number of faces each cherub had.

questions.question: What is the significance of the hands under the wings of the cherubims as described in Ezekiel 10:21?
options: They show the likeness of the hands of a man
They are wings of a lion
questions.correctAnswer: They show the likeness of the hands of a man
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:21 describes that 'the likeness of the hands of a man was under their wings,' indicating a symbolic human element in the cherubim.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 10:22, how did the cherubims move?
options: They went every one straight forward
questions.correctAnswer: They went every one straight forward
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:22 states, 'they went every one straight forward,' clarifying the direction of their movement.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'kavod' in Ezekiel 10:18 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Glory
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'kavod' (כָּבוֹד) in Ezekiel 10:18 means 'glory,' referring to the majestic presence of God departing from the threshold.

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily used in Ezekiel 10:9-10 to describe the wheels?
options: Simile of a wheel within a wheel
questions.correctAnswer: Simile of a wheel within a wheel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:9-10 uses a simile describing the wheels as 'if a wheel had been in the midst of a wheel,' illustrating a complex, interlocking structure.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of divine glory departing as seen in Ezekiel 10:18?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 8:10-11 describes the glory of the LORD filling Solomon’s temple and then departing, paralleling the departure of God's glory in Ezekiel 10:18.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage fulfills the theme of God's presence manifesting with living creatures as in Ezekiel 10?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 4:6-8
questions.explanation: Revelation 4:6-8 describes four living creatures around God's throne, reminiscent of the cherubim in Ezekiel 10, fulfilling the theme of divine presence with living beings.

questions.question: What preceded the glory of the LORD departing from the threshold in Ezekiel 10:18?
options: The cherubims lifting their wings and mounting up
The man clothed with linen scattering coals
The sound of the cherubims’ wings
The appearance of a sapphire throne
questions.correctAnswer: The cherubims lifting their wings and mounting up
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:19 shows the cherubims lifting up their wings and mounting up immediately before the glory of the LORD departs in verse 18, indicating the sequence of events.

questions.question: What Hebrew literary device can be seen in the description of the cherubims having four faces in Ezekiel 10:14?
questions.correctAnswer: Symbolism representing God's attributes
questions.explanation: The four faces of the cherubims symbolize different aspects of God’s creation and attributes, a common Hebrew symbolic device, as seen in Ezekiel 10:14.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 10:12, what is the significance of the eyes all around the wheels and the creatures?
options: They symbolize divine omniscience and vigilance
They are a metaphor for fire
questions.correctAnswer: They symbolize divine omniscience and vigilance
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:12 describes the wheels and creatures full of eyes all around, symbolizing God’s all-seeing nature and constant vigilance.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ezekiel 10:22, the faces of the cherubims in chapter 10 were different from those seen at the river of Chebar.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:22 states that 'the likeness of their faces was the same faces which I saw by the river of Chebar,' confirming they were identical.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 10:5 describes the sound of the cherubims’ wings as being like the voice of the Almighty God when He speaketh.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:5 explicitly states that the sound of the cherubims’ wings was heard as the voice of the Almighty God when He speaketh.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 10 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 10 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 10:4 teach about God's presence in relation to His holiness and judgment?
options: God's glory departs from the temple as a sign of impending judgment
God permanently dwells in the temple regardless of human sin
God's presence is indifferent to human sin and worship
God's glory is hidden behind a veil and inaccessible
questions.correctAnswer: God's glory departs from the temple as a sign of impending judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:4 states that the glory of the LORD went up from the cherub and stood over the threshold, indicating a movement away from the temple, symbolizing God's withdrawal due to judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine communication and revelation is taught in Ezekiel 10:5?
options: God reveals His voice with power and majesty through angelic beings
God communicates silently without any audible signs
God's voice is only heard by the high priest in the temple
God uses natural phenomena only to communicate
questions.correctAnswer: God reveals His voice with power and majesty through angelic beings
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:5 describes the sound of the cherubims’ wings as being like the voice of the Almighty God when He speaks, showing divine majesty in revelation.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the human role in divine judgment is taught in Ezekiel 10:2?
options: God commissions humans as agents to execute His judgment
Humans are excluded from any participation in divine judgment
Judgment is only executed by angels without human involvement
Humans can resist divine judgment through their own power
questions.correctAnswer: God commissions humans as agents to execute His judgment
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 10:2, God commands the man clothed in linen to take coals of fire from between the cherubims and scatter them over the city, showing human participation in divine judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 10:12 specifically demonstrate in the vision of the wheels and cherubim?
questions.correctAnswer: Omniscience
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:12 notes that the bodies and wheels were full of eyes all around, symbolizing God's all-seeing omniscience.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by the phrase 'the glory of the LORD departed from off the threshold of the house' in Ezekiel 10:18?
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:18 shows God's holiness by His departure from the temple threshold, indicating His intolerance of sin in His holy dwelling.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 10:19 connect to the broader biblical theme of divine judgment and exile?
options: It depicts the departure of God's presence, foreshadowing exile
It affirms that God's presence remains with Israel despite exile
It promises immediate restoration of Israel's temple
It symbolizes God's abandonment of all covenant promises
questions.correctAnswer: It depicts the departure of God's presence, foreshadowing exile
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:19 describes the cherubims and wheels lifting up and standing at the east gate with God's glory above, symbolizing God's departure preceding Israel’s exile.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Ezekiel 10:1 make with other biblical theophanies?
options: The sapphire throne vision recalls God’s heavenly sovereignty as in Exodus 24:10
It contradicts all previous depictions of God’s throne
It denies God's presence in heaven
It suggests God’s throne is on earth only
questions.correctAnswer: The sapphire throne vision recalls God’s heavenly sovereignty as in Exodus 24:10
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:1's description of a throne like sapphire parallels Exodus 24:10’s vision of God’s heavenly throne, affirming divine sovereignty.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 10:7 and Ezekiel 10:2 teach about judgment and divine agency?
options: God uses angelic beings and humans as instruments to enact judgment
Judgment is only symbolic and not enacted
Humans alone execute judgment without divine involvement
Judgment is arbitrary and without divine purpose
questions.correctAnswer: God uses angelic beings and humans as instruments to enact judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:2 commands a man clothed in linen to scatter coals from between the cherubims, and 10:7 shows a cherub giving fire to the man, highlighting divine use of both angelic and human agents.

questions.question: What combined theological insight do Ezekiel 10:14 and Ezekiel 10:21 offer about the nature of the cherubim?
options: The cherubim are complex living creatures with multiple faces revealing God's multifaceted nature
The cherubim are simple angels with no symbolic meaning
The cherubim represent idols worshipped by Israel
The cherubim symbolize human kingship alone
questions.correctAnswer: The cherubim are complex living creatures with multiple faces revealing God's multifaceted nature
questions.explanation: Both verses describe cherubim with four faces each, symbolizing diverse divine attributes and functions, indicating their complex nature.

questions.question: What do Ezekiel 10:16 and Ezekiel 10:17 collectively teach about the relationship between the cherubim, wheels, and the Spirit?
options: The spirit animates both cherubim and wheels, symbolizing divine life and unity
The wheels move independently without connection to the cherubim
The cherubim are lifeless symbols without spirit
The wheels represent human power separate from God
questions.correctAnswer: The spirit animates both cherubim and wheels, symbolizing divine life and unity
questions.explanation: Verses 10:16-17 show the wheels moving with the cherubim and both being moved by the spirit of the living creature, indicating unified divine animation.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Ezekiel 10:2-7 depicts mere mythological imagery without theological meaning. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It teaches divine judgment executed through symbolic but real agents, not myth
It is purely a myth with no connection to God's actions
It shows God acting without any purpose or coherence
It indicates God's absence from history
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches divine judgment executed through symbolic but real agents, not myth
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:2-7 describes a man clothed in linen commanded to scatter coals from between cherubims, indicating a real divine judgment act portrayed through rich symbolic vision.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 10:9 teach about divine sovereignty and complexity in God's governance?
options: God's governance is intricate and multidimensional, symbolized by the complex wheels
God's rule is simple and one-dimensional
God's sovereignty is limited by created beings
God's governance depends on human decisions alone
questions.correctAnswer: God's governance is intricate and multidimensional, symbolized by the complex wheels
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:9 describes the wheels as having complex structure and appearance, symbolizing the multifaceted and sovereign nature of God’s governance.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is specifically demonstrated in Ezekiel 10:5 by the sound of the cherubim's wings?
questions.correctAnswer: Omnipotence
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:5 compares the sound of the cherubim’s wings to the voice of Almighty God, demonstrating His omnipotent power.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 10:22 contribute to the narrative arc of God's judgment and mercy in Ezekiel's visions?
options: It shows that the cherubim move straightforwardly, symbolizing God's purposeful judgment and eventual restoration
It depicts confusion and chaos in God's plans
It denies any movement of God’s presence
It suggests God has abandoned His covenant
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that the cherubim move straightforwardly, symbolizing God's purposeful judgment and eventual restoration
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:22 describes the faces and appearances of cherubim moving straight forward, reflecting God’s purposeful and orderly judgment leading to restoration.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 10:8 and Ezekiel 10:21 teach about the incarnation of divine power and human agency?
options: The human hand under the wings symbolizes divine power working through human agency
Divine power is entirely separate from humanity
Divine power is absent in angelic beings
questions.correctAnswer: The human hand under the wings symbolizes divine power working through human agency
questions.explanation: Both verses mention the likeness of a man's hand under the wings of cherubim, symbolizing divine power manifesting through human-like agency.
